readerTitle: Stop asking people to describe the work. Watch them do it.
caseNote: 실제 기업 (Automattic 유급 체험 프로젝트) + 실제 연구 (채용 방법 예측력 메타분석) + 업계 관행 (주방 체험 근무) + 가상 적용 (대기업 내 분석가 채용, 레스토랑 라인 쿡 채용)
insight: 면접은 일에 대한 말을 평가하고, 실무 테스트는 일 자체를 평가한다. 채용 방법이 실제 업무에 가까울수록 추측할 부분이 줄어든다.
misconception: 이력서가 화려하고 면접에서 말을 잘하는 사람이 일도 잘한다.

sources.text: Mullenweg, M. (2014). The CEO of Automattic on Holding "Auditions" to Build a Strong Team. Harvard Business Review, April 2014.
Schmidt, F. L., & Hunter, J. E. (1998). The validity and utility of selection methods in personnel psychology. Psychological Bulletin, 124(2), 262–274.
Sackett, P. R., Zhang, C., Berry, C. M., & Lievens, F. (2022). Revisiting meta-analytic estimates of validity in personnel selection. Journal of Applied Psychology, 107(11), 2040–2068.
레스토랑 업계의 체험 근무(stage) 관행 — 일반적인 업계 관찰

factChecks.note: Automattic이 대부분의 후보자에게 유급 체험 프로젝트(trial)를 거치게 한다는 내용은 Mullenweg의 2014년 HBR 기고에 근거합니다. 시급, 기간, 적용 직군 범위는 시기마다 다를 수 있어 카드에 구체 수치를 넣지 않았습니다. 게시 전 원문과 현재 채용 페이지를 다시 확인하세요.
Schmidt & Hunter(1998)는 실무 테스트를 가장 예측력이 높은 방법 중 하나로 보고했고, Sackett 외(2022) 재분석은 실무 테스트 추정치를 낮추고 구조화 면접을 최상위로 올렸습니다. 카드에는 순위·계수 수치를 넣지 않고 방향만 적었습니다. 표현이 두 논문의 결론과 맞는지 확인하세요.
체험 근무의 임금 지급 의무는 국가·지역마다 다릅니다. 법률 조언을 피하기 위해 카드에는 '규칙이 장소마다 다르다'고만 적었습니다.

cards.title: Stop asking people to describe the work. Watch them do it.
body: Automattic, the company behind WordPress.com, has long hired in an unusual way. Before most candidates get an offer, they do a short, paid trial project: real work, alongside the team.
Its CEO, Matt Mullenweg, called these trials "auditions." He argued they told him far more than a résumé or a conversation ever could.

image.label: A candidate working at a laptop while a team member reviews the work
image.brief: 3D 클레이 스타일. 한 사람이 노트북으로 실제 작업을 하고, 옆에서 팀원이 결과물 화면을 함께 보며 메모하는 장면. 뒤쪽에 무대 커튼 모티프를 살짝 넣어 '오디션' 느낌. 실제 회사 로고나 상표는 쓰지 않음.

cards.title: Three finalists, one analyst job.
body: You lead the operations team inside a large retail company. You need an analyst who can turn messy sales data into clear advice for store managers.
Three finalists all interviewed well. One has a résumé from a famous consulting firm. How do you decide?

options.text: Add a final interview with your senior director
options.feedback: A second opinion helps, but you get more of the same signal: how well people talk about analysis, not how well they do it.

options.text: Give all three the same 90-minute task with sample data, then have them explain their findings
options.feedback: You see the actual skill the job needs, judged on equal terms. It costs everyone a few hours, and that's the trade.

options.text: Hire the consulting-firm candidate. Top firms already screen hard
options.feedback: It saves time, but a famous name tells you someone passed another company's test for another job. It doesn't show they can do yours.

cards.title: Talking about work and doing it are different skills.
body: In his 2014 essay, Mullenweg wrote that résumés and interviews mostly show how people present themselves. A trial shows how they actually work.
During a trial, the team sees things no interview reveals. How does the person handle an unclear brief? Do they ask good questions? How do they write to colleagues they've never met?
For a company where people work remotely and mostly in writing, those were the skills that mattered most.

cards.title: Work sample tests
body: A **work sample test** asks candidates to do a small, realistic piece of the actual job. Then you judge what they produce.
An interview asks, "Tell me how you would do this." A work sample says, "Here, do this." The first measures memory, confidence and storytelling. The second measures the work.

image.label: Two paths: a speech bubble versus a finished piece of work
image.brief: 좌우 비교 인포그래픽. 왼쪽 'Interview: describes the work'에는 말풍선, 오른쪽 'Work sample: does the work'에는 완성된 결과물(차트, 요리 접시, 문서)을 놓음. 오른쪽에 체크 표시를 강조.

cards.title: The closer to the job, the less you guess.
body: Researchers have compared hiring methods for decades. A major 1998 review by Schmidt and Hunter ranked work samples among the best predictors of job performance. Years of experience and unstructured chats did far worse.
A 2022 re-analysis by Sackett and colleagues lowered the estimate for work samples and put **structured interviews** at the top. But work samples still came out well ahead of gut-feel interviews.
The lesson holds: every method is a guess about future work, and doing a slice of it is a good guess.

cards.title: What makes a good test.
body: A useful work sample has a few features:
list: **Real:** a task the person will actually do in the first months
**Same for everyone:** one task, one set of instructions
**Scored on criteria set in advance:** decide what good looks like before you see any answers
**Paid when it's long:** respect for the candidate's time
cards.callout: If you can't describe what good looks like, the test can't tell you who is good.

cards.title: A test has costs, and it can test the wrong thing.
body: Strong candidates with other offers may skip a long unpaid task. Keep tests short, or pay for longer ones. Rules on unpaid trial work vary by place.
A test also measures only the task you picked. If the role itself is poorly defined, you'll pick the wrong task.
And avoid tests that need insider knowledge, like your company's jargon or tools. Those reward people who already worked somewhere like you, not people who can do the work.

cards.title: Now it's a restaurant kitchen.
body: You run a busy bistro and need a line cook for the grill station. Two candidates have solid experience on paper.
Many kitchens already use a trial shift, often called a *stage*. How would you run yours?

options.text: Ask each to cook one dish of their choice for you to taste
options.feedback: You learn they can cook, but they pick their best dish in a calm kitchen. The job is your menu, at speed, during service.

options.text: Pay each for a two-hour shift: prep, then a real station during service, scored by your sous chef on speed, cleanliness and taking direction
options.feedback: It costs a few hours of wages and supervision. In return you see the actual job under real pressure, judged the same way for both.

options.text: Ask each to walk you through how they handle a slammed Friday night
options.feedback: It's quick and free, but a good story about a busy night is not the same as surviving one.

cards.title: Judge the work, not the description of it.
body: A short, realistic, fairly scored task shows you what no résumé or conversation can.
**Try it today:** pick one role you hire for. Write down a task a new hire does in week one that could fit into 90 minutes. Then write three things a great result would include.
